hints.junior: Flex items have an invisible default: min-width: auto. For an item with a long word or filename inside, that means 'never smaller than my own content' — flex-shrink can't override it.
hints.mid: min-width: auto resolves to the item's content-intrinsic width, not zero. flex-shrink only controls how items shrink relative to each other once they hit that floor — it doesn't remove the floor.
hints.staff: This is the CSS Flexbox spec's automatic minimum size rule for the main axis, identical across evergreen browsers — not a bug, just an easy-to-miss default almost nobody sets deliberately.

hints.junior: Same three-card row, same long filename. Broken mode pushes the row wider than its container; fixed mode truncates the text with an ellipsis and the row stays put.
hints.mid: Only min-width changes between the two states — flex-shrink is identical in both. Shrink was always willing to act, it just had nowhere to go until the floor was removed.
hints.staff: Inspect the middle card's computed min-width in DevTools in each state: auto (resolving to content width) vs 0px — the entire behavioral difference in one property.

hints.junior: flex-shrink is 'how eager is this item to shrink'; min-width: auto is 'how small will it ever actually go.' Even an eager shrinker stops at its content's own width unless you remove that floor.
hints.mid: min-width: 0 removes the floor entirely, letting flex-shrink act all the way down to zero. Pair it with overflow: hidden and text-overflow: ellipsis on the inner content so it truncates instead of clipping mid-character.
hints.staff: The same rule applies on the cross axis for column layouts (min-height: 0), and Grid has an equivalent gotcha: minmax(0, 1fr) vs. a plain 1fr track, for exactly the same automatic-minimum-size reason.

hints.junior: The same fix, same reasoning, applies to flex-direction: column layouts — use min-height: 0 instead of min-width: 0, for the same reason on the other axis.
hints.mid: CSS Grid's version of this bug: a plain 1fr track can still refuse to shrink below its content's intrinsic size. minmax(0, 1fr) is the grid equivalent of min-width: 0 on a flex item.
hints.staff: Nested flex containers compound this: a parent item's own min-width: auto sets the floor for its whole subtree, regardless of what's declared on children further down — audit outside-in when hunting this in a deeply nested layout.

anecdotes.junior: A dashboard I built looked perfect in dev with short test data. In production, one user had a long filename in a flex card and the whole row overflowed sideways. One line, min-width: 0, fixed it.
anecdotes.mid: It's a classic 'passes code review, fails in production' bug: the layout is visually correct with realistic-looking short test content. The failure only appears with content wider than the container, which nobody deliberately tests for.
anecdotes.staff: The nested case is worse: if a parent flex item is also missing min-width: 0, none of its children's own shrink behavior can fix an overflow — the parent's auto-minimum sets the floor for the whole subtree. Audit outside-in, not inside-out.
